candidates.title: Learning Agent Execution for KV-Cache Management in Agentic Serving
candidates.reason: CacheScout learns agent execution transitions online and uses them for KV-cache eviction and proactive prefetching. It directly connects agent workflow semantics to serving-time KV management and follows naturally from the newly added AgentSysBench workload characterization.
evidence: Implemented as an agent-aware KV-cache runtime layer on top of vLLM without requiring predefined workflow graphs or offline training.

Reports KV-cache hit-rate gains of 10–18 percentage points, mean TTFT reductions of 18–45%, per-turn latency reductions of 29–38%, and peak throughput gains up to 57% across representative multi-agent workloads.

candidates.title: Elastic KV Cache for LLM Serving: A Working Reclamation Mechanism, and Why Chunked Prefill Already Closes the Gap
candidates.reason: Builds a CUDA virtual-memory mechanism that dynamically lends prefill-reserve memory to the KV pool, then reports a useful negative result showing that smaller chunked prefill often recovers more KV with nearly equal latency. This is valuable for avoiding unnecessary complexity in serving-memory designs.
evidence: Uses two physical handles mapped into one contiguous virtual range per layer and keeps the attention kernel unchanged; decommit/recommit is performed dynamically without out-of-memory failures.
Controlled long-prompt experiments find about 1% median TTFT difference between chunk sizes 8192 and 32768, while reserve value shrinks from 16% of KV at TP1 to 2.7% at TP4.
